subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename workspace files in bootstrap-extra-files, or keep the hook restricted to recognized bootstrap filenames?
rationale: This defines which workspace files can enter deterministic session bootstrap context and touches the config/system-prompt safety boundary, while current main intentionally documents recognized-only behavior.

options.title: Approve bounded hook contract
options.body: Allow custom basenames only through explicit configuration after the candidate PR or replacement preserves guards, budgets, filtering, ordering, and docs.

options.title: Keep recognized basenames only
options.body: Reject arbitrary workspace-file injection and use narrower first-class filename proposals for any approved new bootstrap concepts.

options.title: Defer to broader context API
options.body: Leave the allowlist in place until maintainers design a broader context-loading contract for discovery, trust, and session scoping.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded hook contract
recommendation.body: Allow custom basenames only through explicit configuration after the candidate PR or replacement preserves guards, budgets, filtering, ordering, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent boundary-safe bootstrap file-loading refactor makes him the strongest available owner for the contract and guard discussion.
